title: Apache HTTP Server Examples
description: Small Apache HTTP Server examples from the lessons. Each example links back to its explanation and practice task.

examples.title: An HTTP server sends responses
examples.description: Apache HTTP Server accepts web requests and sends responses. For a static site, the response body often comes straight from a file.
examples.code:
Request: GET /club.html
Response status: 200 if the file is served
Response body: the HTML file

examples.title: Listen on a practice port
examples.description: Listen selects the address and port where Apache accepts connections. Bind a local experiment to loopback.

examples.title: Virtual hosts choose a site
examples.description: A virtual host groups configuration for a site. ServerName identifies the intended host name.

examples.title: Directory access is explicit
examples.description: A Directory block applies settings to a filesystem directory. Access rules should expose only intended public files.

examples.title: Choose the first page
examples.description: DirectoryIndex lists candidate files for a directory request. The first existing suitable file can be used.

examples.title: Understand URL and file paths
examples.description: A URL path and a filesystem path are different. DocumentRoot usually provides the base used to map a URL path to a file.

examples.title: MIME types describe files
examples.description: A MIME type tells the browser what kind of response it is receiving. Apache uses configured mappings and modules for common file types.
examples.code:
CSS: text/css
JSON: application/json
HTML: text/html

examples.title: Modules add features
examples.description: Apache modules add features such as headers, rewriting or TLS. A directive may require its matching module to be loaded.

examples.title: Read htaccess limits
examples.description: An .htaccess file can apply permitted directory settings when the server allows overrides. It is not always enabled or needed.
examples.code:
Server-level choice: AllowOverride None
Result: .htaccess overrides are not used for that directory

examples.title: Custom error documents
examples.description: ErrorDocument can point to a local page that explains a status such as not found.

examples.title: Logs explain requests and problems
examples.description: Apache access logs record request information. Error logs help diagnose server failures or configuration problems.
examples.code:
Access log question: which URL was requested?
Error log question: why could the server not read the file?

examples.title: Check before changing a server
examples.description: Validate the configuration before an approved reload, then test real routes and assets. A syntax check does not prove the whole website works.
